dedupe_keys.name: 20 years fee for service utilization by health service code

description: The source describes Alberta physician fee-for-service utilisation by health service code, with an XLSX workbook labelled fiscal 1995–1996 through 2014–2015. Tables report services and payments for registered AHCIP members and exclude care outside Alberta or Canada. Two companions provide local-area and health-zone breakdowns for fiscal 2011–2012 through 2014–2015. Four others cover age/sex, functional centre/site type, service code and specialty by service code, with distinct rolling windows within 2008–2015. A specialty package labels descriptors XLSX while some URLs end in .xls. Three further companions report daily patients/claims/payments by zone and specialty, fee-for-service averages by specialty and the top-20 fee codes by expenditure. Their XLSX descriptors span differing windows within 2008–2015. The specialty-averages native start is 2010, while descriptors include 2008–2009; this conflict is preserved. The curated family retains separate source identities, fields and periods without claiming interchangeable tables or continuous common coverage. Exact units and within-year resolution are unstated except for source-described daily averages. The Canadian Urban Data Catalogue supplies full descriptions and original Alberta identities. It names Open Government Licence - Alberta; the original Alberta metadata endpoint returned HTTP 403 during review. Costs, present file availability, numerical contents and specific simulation applications remain unverified. No workbook, document or dataset body was retrieved. Related source tables retain distinct identities. A further source-defined fee-for-service companion reports payments, services and patients by physician specialty. Five XLSX descriptors span fiscal 2009–2010 through 2014–2015. It retains the exclusion of services outside Alberta or Canada. This aggregate specialty table is distinct from the specialty-by-service-code component; no equality of their totals was tested.
